properties.description: Ruthenium doped or supported NiFe LDH

nodes.source_text: The electrochemical performance of Ru/d-NiFe LDH toward HER was evaluated in an N₂-saturated 1 M KOH solution under a typical three-electrode system.[29] It has exhibited very low overpotentials of 18 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² (η₁₀) and 73 mV at 50 mA cm⁻² (η₅₀)... Ru/d-NiFe LDH catalyst displays the highest C_dl of 36.67 mF dec⁻¹... chronopotentiometry measurements at 10, 50, and 100 mA cm⁻²... outstanding durability

As for alkaline OER, the Ru/d-NiFe LDH catalyst has also exhibited superior OER activity with an ultralow η₁₀ of 220 mV together with a small Tafel slope of 60.48 mV dec⁻¹... Ru/d-NiFe LDH catalyst has possessed the highest C_dl value of 28.48 mF cm⁻²... i-t curves delivering at 10, 50, and 100 mA cm⁻² for 150 h were recorded... Negligible attenuation of current density

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: a two-electrode electrolyzer was assembled for overall water splitting by both-side paring the Ru/d-NiFe LDH catalyst... It only requires an ultralow cell voltage of 1.49 and 1.63 V to reach current densities of 10 and 50 mA cm⁻²... the high Faradaic efficiency (≈99.8%)... outstanding long-term stability without obvious current decay under 100 mA cm⁻² for 140 h

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH seawater
nodes.source_text: In 1 M KOH seawater electrolyte... the Ru/d-NiFe LDH catalyst requires a low HER η₁₀ of merely 28 mV with a small Tafel slope of 57.3 mV dec⁻¹

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH seawater
nodes.source_text: the Ru/d-NiFe LDH also showed superior OER η₁₀ of 272 mV with fast kinetics (40.1 mV dec⁻¹) in seawater

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1 M KOH seawater
nodes.source_text: we also assembled the Ru/d-NiFe LDH as both anode and cathode to test the alkaline seawater electrolysis performance... The Ru/d-NiFe LDH paired cell can deliver small applied voltages of 1.66 and 1.78 V, respectively, at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻² along with a long-term durability of 100 h in 1 M KOH seawater

nodes.description: HER comparison with reference catalysts in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: superior to that of bare NF (307 mV_η₁₀ / 470 mV_η₅₀), NiFe LDH (169 mV_η₁₀ / 348 mV_η₅₀), d-NiFe LDH (127 mV_η₁₀ / 253 mV_η₅₀), Ru/NiFe LDH (39 mV_η₁₀ / 107 mV_η₅₀), and even the Pt/C benchmark (25 mV_η₁₀ / 88 mV_η₅₀)

nodes.description: OER comparison with reference catalysts in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: outperform the counterparts... including bare NF (415 mV, 105.09 mV dec⁻¹), NiFe LDH (294 mV, 80.16 mV dec⁻¹), d-NiFe LDH (243 mV, 113.84 mV dec⁻¹), Ru/NiFe LDH (323 mV_η50 144.78 mV dec⁻¹), and commercial RuO₂ catalyst (336 mV, 84.32 mV dec⁻¹)

nodes.characterization_summary: d-NiFe LDH shows interconnected nanosheets vertically grown on NF with smooth surface; Ru/d-NiFe LDH maintains vertically aligned nanosheet morphology but with rougher surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2b and Figures S5,S6, Supporting Information, the interconnected d-NiFe LDH nanosheets were vertically grown on NF with a smooth surface and a lateral size of several hundred nanometers... After the introduction of the Ru source, the Ru/d-NiFe LDH still maintained the vertically aligned nanosheet morphology but with a rougher surface for beneficial catalyst/electrolyte interaction (Figure 2c,d).

properties.description: nanofiber network with interwoven fibrous morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/d-NiFe LDH shows interconnected, porous nanosheet morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image of Ru/d-NiFe LDH in Figure 2e,f clearly illustrates the interconnected, porous nanosheet morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/d-NiFe LDH shows d-spacings of 0.207 nm (Ru (101)) and 0.223 nm (NiFe LDH (015)); d-NiFe LDH shows d-spacing of 0.250 nm ((012) plane).
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image in Figure 2g, the well-resolved d-spacings of 0.207 and 0.223 nm can be indexed to the Ru (101) and NiFe LDH (015) planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/d-NiFe LDH identifies (200)/(101) crystal planes of Ru and (116) crystal plane of NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the selected area electron diffraction pattern (SAED) of Ru/d-NiFe LDH, we can clearly identify the (200)/(101) crystal planes of Ru and (116) crystal plane of NiFe LDH (Figure 2h).

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, Ru, and O over Ru/d-NiFe LDH nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping in Figure 2i further confirms the homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, Ru, and O over the entire nanosheets.
Furtherly, the mass ratios of Ru/Ni/Fe in Ru/d-NiFe LDH were examined about 2.06: 90.16: 7.78 by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS, Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH characteristic peaks at 11.32°, 22.82°, 33.59°, 34.24°, 38.63°, 45.90°, 59.72°, 60.97° assigned to (003), (006), (101), (012), (015), (018), (110), (113) planes; Ru/d-NiFe LDH peaks slightly shift to smaller angles, no Ru peaks due to low 2.06 wt% Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) was employed to examine the phase structure of the as-prepared samples, as shown in Figure 2j.

nodes.characterization_summary: LDH peaks at 456 cm⁻¹ (e_g bending) and 537 cm⁻¹ (A_1g stretching); Ru/d-NiFe LDH shows decreased peak strength indicating Ru-d-NiFe LDH interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2k compares the Raman spectra of as-synthesized catalysts. Two representative Raman peaks at 456 and 537 cm⁻¹ are ascribed to the e_g bending and A_lg stretching modes of the LDH structure, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/d-NiFe LDH shows peaks at 1396.9, 2361.7 cm⁻¹ (C-H), 1640.2, 3131.4 cm⁻¹ (O-H) with higher O-H intensity indicating better hydrophilicity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) was carried out to examine the surface groups of these catalysts (Figure 2l).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/d-NiFe LDH Ni 2p: 855.5/873.3 eV (Ni²⁺), 856.9/874.7 eV (Ni³⁺) with increased Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ ratio; Ru 3p: 462.4/484.9 eV (Ru⁰), 465.1/488.4 eV (Ru-O) with +0.26 eV shift; O 1s: oxygen vacancy at 531.5 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a presents the Ni 2p XPS spectra... For the Ru/d-NiFe LDH NSs, the peaks around 855.5 and 873.3 eV could be assigned to Ni²⁺... Figure 3b presents the Ru 3p XPS spectra featuring the mixed states of metallic Ru (≈462.4 and 484.9 eV) and Ru-O species (≈465.1 and 488.4 eV)... Figure 3d compares the O1s XPS spectra... the rich oxygen vacancy (531.5 eV) in the Ru/d-NiFe LDH samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/d-NiFe LDH shows high EPR signal intensity at g = 2.005 indicating abundant oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the surface defects information was checked by room-temperature electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra in Figure 3c.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/d-NiFe LDH Ru K-edge slightly blue-shifted vs Ru/NiFe LDH; average Ru valences +2.23 (Ru/d-NiFe LDH) and +1.99 (Ru/NiFe LDH).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectrum was utilized to study the local electronic structure and coordination environment of Ru sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/d-NiFe LDH shows Ru-Ru and Ru-O coordination peaks shifted to lower R-value indicating lattice distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) analysis was employed to investigate the local coordination environment.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/d-NiFe LDH shows larger weight loss (-20.32 wt%) than d-NiFe LDH (-7.75 wt%) due to removal of absorbed water.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As indicated by the thermogravimetry (TGA) curves in Figure S11, Supporting Information, the Ru/d-NiFe LDH demonstrates a larger weight loss (-20.32 wt%) than that of d-NiFe LDH (-7.75 wt%) due to the remove of absorbed water.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/d-NiFe LDH contact angle 9.8° vs d-NiFe LDH 19.5°, indicating better hydrophilicity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the Ru/d-NiFe LDH shows a smaller contact angle (CA, 9.8°) and better hydrophilicity relative to d-NiFe LDH (19.5°), as presented in Figure S12, Supporting Information.
